analyzed_vuln.description: The variadic formatting-parameter constructor unconditionally calls `this->set_parameters(m_data)`. When the format call has no arguments, `m_data` is `AK::Array<TypeErasedParameter, 0>`; AK::Array represents storage as `T __data[Size]`, so the zero-sized specialization has no valid standard C++ array/object storage. Converting/accessing that member to form the empty span triggers UBSan's insufficient-space member-call error at Format.h:298. The ASN.1 parser merely exposes this latent zero-argument formatting bug by calling `dbgln("FIXME: Implement UTCTime with offset!")`; the unsafe zero-parameter handling in `VariadicFormatParams`, rather than UTC date parsing, is the root location.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Fuzzer bytes are passed directly by `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` to `TLS::Certificate::parse_asn1`. They must decode far enough as an X.509 certificate to reach a validity value tagged UTCTime, and that value must pass the parser's required numeric YYMMDDhhmm[ss] fields while using a syntactically accepted `+hhmm` or `-hhmm` timezone offset. This sets `offset_hours`/`offset_minutes` and reaches the no-substitution-argument `dbgln` at ASN1.cpp:165. Instantiating `dbgln<>` then constructs `VariadicFormatParams<..., /* zero Parameters */>`, and its access/conversion of `Array<TypeErasedParameter, 0>` triggers the reported UB. More generally, any reached zero-argument formatting call using this template can trigger the same defect.
